correctness.rationale: For every convex window and sufficiently small disjoint interior disks, every generic line intersection starts as one interval and each disk it crosses adds one component. Cauchy width integration normalizes invariant lines by perimeter. Each pairwise jointly hit offset set has length max(2r-d|cos(theta)|,0), integrating exactly to 2d[s asin(s)+sqrt(1-s^2)-1]. Positive arcsine coefficients give inverse odd-distance moments; the finite positive Hankel measure supported at distinct reciprocal squared distances is identified by 2M moments, including collision multiplicities. A self-contained checker passed five independent angular integrals, twelve positive finite-jet coefficients with three independent direct-versus-series evaluations, exact Hankel reconstruction with one repeated pair distance, and conditioned-line Monte Carlo.

value.rationale: A single unlabeled scalar statistic of random line-section topology, observed as the common disk-hole radius varies, reconstructs all pair distances of an arbitrary finite planar point set with a finite number of Taylor coefficients; the constructive positive-Hankel inversion handles repetitions. This is a motivated inverse geometric problem, independent of the surrounding convex window except perimeter. It goes substantially beyond a single trivial first-hit count, while carefully not claiming center-coordinate recovery or noisy stability.
